references.text: Moses calls Israel a 'perverse and crooked generation' (Deut 32:5), using the same language as Jesus does here with 'faithless and twisted generation' (γενεὰ ... διεστραμμένη).
The Lord calls Israel 'a perverse generation' and children without faithfulness, which reflects Jesus' expression 'faithless and twisted generation'.

God refers to the people of Israel as a 'wicked congregation' that grumbles against Him, asking how long He must endure them—parallel to Jesus' question, 'How long shall I be with you and bear with you?'
Isaiah speaks of God carrying and enduring His people; Jesus' words 'how long shall I bear with you' (ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν) reflect a similar divine patience toward a rebellious people.
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says, 'You faithless and twisted generation! How long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you?'—the same event and nearly identical wording.
The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus says, 'You faithless generation! How long shall I be with you? How long shall I endure you?'—the same event at the foot of the Mount of Transfiguration.
Paul uses the expression 'a crooked and twisted generation' (γενεᾶς σκολιᾶς καὶ διεστραμμένης), which is closely related to Jesus' wording here and alludes to Deut 32:5.
Peter urges the people to be saved from this 'crooked generation' (γενεᾶς τῆς σκολιᾶς), addressing the same theme of a twisted generation that Jesus confronted.
The Lord asks Moses, 'How long will this people despise me, and how long will they refuse to believe in me?'—parallel to Jesus' frustration over the people's unbelief.
